elements.section: Give emergency contraception if patient had unprotected sex in past 5 days and does not want pregnancy:
elements.text: Check pregnancy test and if negative, insert Copper IUD1 as soon as possible or give single dose levonorgestrel 1.5mg orally.

elements.section: Give emergency contraception if patient had unprotected sex in past 5 days and does not want pregnancy:
elements.text: If patient > 80kg, BMI2 ≥ 30, or on efavirenz, rifampicin, phenytoin or carbamazepine, offer Copper IUD1 or increase dose of levonorgestrel to 3mg.

elements.section: Give emergency contraception if patient had unprotected sex in past 5 days and does not want pregnancy:
elements.text: If patient on ketoconazole/fluconazole, advise levonorgestrel may cause nausea/vomiting and offer Copper IUD1 instead.

elements.section: Give emergency contraception if patient had unprotected sex in past 5 days and does not want pregnancy:
elements.text: If patient vomits < 2 hours after taking levonorgestrel, repeat dose.

elements.section: Give emergency contraception if patient had unprotected sex in past 5 days and does not want pregnancy:
elements.text: Offer to start long-term contraceptive at same visit (if IUD not chosen). If injectable or implant given, check pregnancy test in 2 weeks.

elements.section: Give emergency contraception if patient had unprotected sex in past 5 days and does not want pregnancy:
elements.text: Assess for HIV and hepatitis B post-exposure prophylaxis 119. Advise patient to return for pregnancy test if next period is more than 7 days late.
CONTRACEPTION
1The levonorgestrel IUD 52mg (LNG-IUD) is not coded for emergency contraception. 2BMI = weight (kg) ÷ height (m) ÷ height (m). 3If patient > 40 years old, check breasts 6 monthly.
Assess the patient starting and using contraception
Assess When to assess Note
Symptoms Every visit Check for symptoms of STIs: vaginal discharge, ulcers, lower abdominal pain. If present 62. Manage other symptoms as on symptom pages.
Long-term health conditions

First visit Check suitability of method if any of: cancer (especially breast, cervical, uterine), blood clots, hypertension, stroke, ischaemic heart disease, diabetes, liver disease, migraines, or unexplained vaginal bleeding 172.
Medication Every visit If on ART, TB treatment or antiseizure medication, check method is suitable 172.
Periods Every visit Ask about interval between periods, blood loss, number of days period lasts, dysmenorrhoea (pain/cramps associated with periods).
Menopause If > 40 years: yearly Ask about menopausal symptoms: hot flushes, night sweats, vaginal dryness, mood changes, difficulty sleeping. If menopausal 187.
Sexual health Every visit If risky sexual behaviour (new or multiple partner/s, uses condoms unreliably, has sex under influence of alcohol/drugs), give safe sex advice.

Adherence Every visit • If using contraceptive, ask about concerns and satisfaction with method. If unsatisfied, consider different contraceptive, rather than risking unwanted pregnancy. • If patient has missed injections or pills, manage 171.
Side effects Every visit If already on contraceptive, ask about and manage side effects 171.
Weight (BMI2) Every visit BMI = weight (kg) ÷ height (m) ÷ height (m). Aim for BMI of 18 to < 25. If BMI ≥ 25 156.
BP First visit; every visit if on pill or injectable
• Check BP: if ≥ 140/90 148. • If known hypertension or BP ≥ 140/90, avoid/change from combined oral contraceptive. If BP ≥ 160/100, also avoid/change from injectable.
Breasts First visit, then yearly3 Check for lumps in breasts and axillae. If lumps in breasts 55; if lumps in axillae 42.
Pregnancy Every visit Before starting contraception or if pregnancy suspected (nausea/breast tenderness/missed period when using combined oral contraceptive), check for pregnancy 174.
HIV Every visit Test for HIV 124. If positive, give routine HIV care 126. If negative, consider need for PrEP 119.

Cervical screen When needed If HIV negative: start screening at 25 years, repeat every 10 years 70. If HIV positive: start screening at 25 years, regardless of when ART was started, repeat every 5 years 70.

Advise the patient starting/on contraception • Educate patient to use contraceptive reliably. Advise to discuss concerns/problems with method and find an alternative, rather than stopping it and risking unwanted pregnancy. • Recommend dual contraception: one method of contraception plus condoms to protect from STIs and HIV. Demonstrate and give male/female condoms. • Discuss risky sexual behaviour. Explain risks of pregnancy and infections. Encourage patient to have 1 partner at a time and if HIV negative, to test for HIV between partners. Advise that partner/s test too. • Educate about the availability of emergency contraception (see above) and termination of pregnancy 175 to prevent unwanted pregnancy. Also educate about PrEP. • Advise patient on pill/implant to tell clinician if starting ART, TB treatment or antiseizure medication as these may interfere with pill/implant effectiveness. • If on pill: if vomits within 2 hours/severe diarrhoea within 12 hours of taking pill, repeat dose as soon as possible. If persistent vomiting/diarrhoea > 24 hours, advise to use condoms or abstain during illness and for 7 days after.
